observations: Photo 0 shows a large dark solar panel standing vertically on dirt ground with a visible grid of cells.
Photo 1 shows the same panel from a similar angle with “INNOSON GLOBAL GROUP” watermarked across the center.
Other solar panels are stacked or leaning in the background of both photos.
No readable wattage, brand, or model label is visible on the panel face in either photo.
The panel appears to be a standard framed photovoltaic module.

claims.evidence: Photos show a panel but no test data, labels, or quality marks are readable.

risks.risk: Wattage and electrical output are unknown; the panel may be low-wattage or non-functional.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rear label/sticker showing wattage, voltage, and model, or a video of the panel connected to a charge controller/meter producing power.
risks.if_unproven: as an untested panel of unknown wattage

risks.risk: Physical defects such as microcracks, delamination, or water ingress are not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: Close-up video or photos of the panel surface, corners, frame, and junction box.

risks.risk: The item may not be the exact panel pictured if the seller uses stock images.
risks.proof: Video showing the panel in the seller’s location with a handwritten note or today’s date.

proof_requests: Close-up of the back label showing wattage, brand, and model
Video of the panel producing power under sunlight or connected to a tester
Close-up footage of the panel surface and frame for cracks or damage
response.reason: The photos clearly show a solar panel, so it can be identified by type and priced at its worst case as an untested unit of unknown wattage.
